{{< include _bayesammi-macros.txt >}}

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# HTML figures are drawn as PNG and kept as WebP: lossless (the same pixels in about half the space of PNG), or
# lossy at quality 90 when that is less than half the size, as for traces and densities of thousands of draws. The
# PDF figures stay vector graphics. Any failure of magick (not installed, no WebP, or a broken installation whose
# system libraries are missing) keeps the PNG
webp <- function(path) {
  if (knitr::is_latex_output() || !grepl(pattern = "[.]png$", x = path)) return(path)
  tryCatch(
      {
        if (!requireNamespace("magick", quietly = TRUE) || !isTRUE(magick::magick_config()$webp)) return(path)
        img <- magick::image_read(path)
        out <- sub(pattern = "[.]png$", replacement = ".webp", x = path)
        tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".webp")
        magick::image_write(
            image   = img
          , path    = out
          , format  = "webp"
          , quality = 100
          , defines = c(`webp:lossless` = "true")
          )
        magick::image_write(image = img, path = tmp, format = "webp", quality = 90)
        if (file.size(tmp) < file.size(out) / 2) file.copy(from = tmp, to = out, overwrite = TRUE)
        unlink(c(path, tmp))
        out
      }
    , error = function(e) path
    )
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = FALSE, comment = "", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5,
                      dev = if (knitr::is_latex_output()) "cairo_pdf" else "ragg_png", dpi = 96,
                      fig.process = webp)
if (requireNamespace("bayesammi", quietly = TRUE)) library(bayesammi) else
  pkgload::load_all(export_all = FALSE, helpers = FALSE, quiet = TRUE)
```

# Abstract

Posterior summaries are valid only after the chains have reached their stationary distribution and are long enough.
Crossa et al. (2011) used three diagnostics: Raftery and Lewis (1995), Heidelberger and Welch (1983) and Gelman and
Rubin (1992). `bayes_ammi()` computes all three, together with effective sample sizes, through the package
**coda**.

# Several chains

```{r fit}
fit <-
  bayes_ammi(
      .data   = Maiz
    , .y      = y
    , .gen    = entry
    , .env    = site
    , .rep    = rep
    , .nIter  = 4000
    , .k      = 2
    , .burnin = 1000
    , .thin   = 1
    , .chains = 3
    , .priors = bam_priors(
          mu_mean     = 0
        , mu_var      = 1e+8
        , tau_mean    = 0
        , tau_var     = 1e+8
        , delta_mean  = 0
        , delta_var   = 1e+8
        , lambda_mean = 0
        , lambda_var  = 1e+8
        , nu          = 1
        , s2          = NULL
        )
    , .level  = 0.95
    , .seed   = 5
    , .align  = TRUE
    , .model  = "AMMI"
    , .het    = FALSE
    , .waic   = TRUE
    )
```

The first chain starts at the least-squares fit and the others at dispersed values (singular values scaled by
factors between 0.5 and 1.5, perturbed scores, error variance scaled between 0.5 and 2).

# Traces

```{r trace, fig.height = 6}
plot(x = fit, which = "trace", pars = c("mu", "sigma2", "lambda[1]", "lambda[2]", "alpha[8,1]"))
```

# Gelman-Rubin

The potential scale reduction factor compares the variance between chains with the variance within them. Values
below 1.1 (better, 1.01) indicate that the chains have mixed.

```{r gelman}
fit$diagnostics$gelman
summary(object = fit$summary$rhat)
```

# Raftery-Lewis

The dependence factor $I$ measures how much longer the chain must be than an independent sample of the same
precision; $I > 5$ indicates strong autocorrelation.

```{r raftery}
fit$diagnostics$raftery[[1]]
```

# Heidelberger-Welch

The stationarity test is applied to the whole chain, then after dropping the first 10%, 20%, ... of it. The
half-width test asks whether the mean is estimated precisely enough. Each test has level 0.05, so among many
parameters a few failures are expected by chance.

```{r heidel}
fit$diagnostics$heidel[[1]]
```

# Effective sample size and Monte Carlo error

```{r ess}
fit$summary[block %in% c("mu", "sigma2", "lambda"), list(parameter, mean, sd, mc_se, ess, rhat)]
```

The Monte Carlo standard error `mc_se` is $\mathrm{sd}/\sqrt{\mathrm{ess}}$. Run longer chains when it is
not small compared with the precision you need. The weak second singular value mixes more slowly than the other
parameters.

# The draws for further analysis

`fit$draws` is a `coda::mcmc.list`, so every function of **coda** applies:

```{r coda}
coda::autocorr.diag(mcmc.obj = fit$draws[, c("lambda[1]", "lambda[2]")], lags = c(1, 5, 10))
```

# posterior and bayesplot

The draws also convert to a `draws_df` of **posterior**, which gives the rank-normalised $\widehat{R}$ and the bulk
and tail effective sample sizes of Vehtari et al. (2021), and the plots of **bayesplot** take the `mcmc.list` directly
(Gabry et al. 2019):

```{r posterior}
dr <- posterior::as_draws_df(x = fit)
posterior::summarise_draws(
    .x = posterior::subset_draws(x = dr, variable = c("mu", "sigma2", "lambda[1]", "lambda[2]"))
  , "mean", "sd", "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail"
  )
```

```{r bayesplot, fig.height = 3.4}
bayesplot::mcmc_rank_overlay(x = fit$draws, pars = c("lambda[1]", "lambda[2]"))
```

Rank plots are flat and overlapping when the chains mix well.

# Interpretation of convergence

```{r int}
bam_interpret(
    x             = fit
  , higher_better = TRUE
  , top           = 5
  )$findings[1:2]
```

Gelman, A. and Rubin, D. B. (1992). Inference from iterative simulation using multiple sequences. *Statistical Science*, 7(4), 457--472.

Raftery, A. E. and Lewis, S. M. (1995). The number of iterations, convergence diagnostics and generic Metropolis algorithms. In W. R. Gilks, D. J. Spiegelhalter and S. Richardson (eds), *Practical Markov Chain Monte Carlo*. Chapman and Hall, London.

Heidelberger, P. and Welch, P. D. (1983). Simulation run length control in the presence of an initial transient. *Operations Research*, 31(6), 1109--1144.

Plummer, M., Best, N., Cowles, K. and Vines, K. (2006). CODA: convergence diagnosis and output analysis for MCMC. *R News*, 6(1), 7--11.

Vehtari, A., Gelman, A., Simpson, D., Carpenter, B. and Burkner, P.-C. (2021). Rank-normalization, folding, and localization: an improved R-hat for assessing convergence of MCMC. *Bayesian Analysis*, 16(2), 667--718.

Gabry, J., Simpson, D., Vehtari, A., Betancourt, M. and Gelman, A. (2019). Visualization in Bayesian workflow. *Journal of the Royal Statistical Society A*, 182(2), 389--402.
